model_annotation: Figure 3(a) is a line plot illustrating training loss as a function of training steps for multiple methods, with the goal of showing how the loss curves evolve over time under different model variants. The x-axis is labeled “Steps” and appears to use a linear scale spanning from 0 to 150k, with tick marks at approximately 0, 50k, 100k, and 150k. The y-axis is labeled “Loss” on a linear scale, spanning roughly from about 2.4 up to about 3.4, with evenly spaced tick labels at approximately 2.4, 2.6, 2.8, 3.0, 3.2, and 3.4. The plot contains six solid lines without visible point markers: a blue line (Vanilla) that starts near the top of the axis (around 3.4 at step 0) and decreases steeply early, then continues decreasing more gradually to about 2.65 by 150k; an orange line (StrmLLM, n=64) that begins similarly high (around 3.4) and declines in the same general pattern to roughly 2.60–2.62 by 150k; a green line (SepLLM, n=64) that drops from around 3.4 to approximately 2.58–2.60 by 150k; a red line (SepLLM, n=64, H/T) that also starts near 3.4 and decreases to about 2.56–2.58 at 150k; a purple line (SepLLM, n=128) that follows a similar downward trajectory and ends near about 2.57–2.59 at 150k; and a brown line (SepLLM, n=256) that likewise decreases from about 3.4 and finishes around 2.55–2.57 by the end of the step range, with all curves showing a rapid initial drop followed by a slower decline as steps increase.
